Despite initial hopes that inhi- bition of lipoxygenase might prove of benefit in patients with ul- cerative colitis,1 a study in those with mild or moderately active relapsing disease found that the symptomatic benefits of zileuton were confined to those not already receiving sulfasalazine.2 A subsequent study showed zileuton was not significantly better than placebo in maintaining remission.3 For a discussion of in- flammatory bowel disease and its management, see p.1697. 1. A study in 8 patients with allergic rhinitis (p.565) found that a single dose of zileuton 800 mg reduced the response to a nasal antigen challenge 3 hours later,1 including reduced sneezing and nasal congestion. 1.
